liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): The opener was fired up, leading into a standard first set with a nice Cassidy; After the second verse, Jerry scrambles eggs and passionately sings the Wichita cut line [21][23][26]
- **Eyes of the World** (2 reviews): The song is played faster than normal, with everyone contributing energy; This specific version of the song is considered the best available recording [26][29]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Jerry Garcia was heard growling at one point during the performance [22]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): The song rocks hard, with the drummer and keyboardist contributing to the groove [25]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The transition into Fire on the Mountain is described as a standout performance [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-16.sbd.unknown.20085.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1978-04-16.148386.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.fixed.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 157 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1978-04-16.149552.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 155 min [5]
- **gd1978-04-16.148566.sony.54p.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 161 min [6]
- **gd1978-04-16.sbd.cantor.motb.81457.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 144 min; rated 4.61/5 by 46 [9]
- **gd78-04-16.sbd.lai.292.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 144 min; rated 4.53/5 by 40 [10]. Said about its sound: Recording features slight digital noise, possibly from a misaligned DAT head in its history; Digital static is present on the final two songs of the recording; Digital noise is annoying but not severe enough to prevent downloading the file [18][19][22]

## Around the show

- One of only two Grateful Dead shows played in the reviewer's home state of West Virginia [21]
- Reviewer is a Huntington native who sought this show as their first tape trade [24]
- Reviewer was fourteen years old at the time and did not get into the band later [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-16.sbd.unknown.20085.shnf**: source: Master Reel> PCM> ??> DAT> Sonic Solutions> CD [1]
- **gd1978-04-16.148386.betty.dalton.miller.sirmick.fixed.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor;Tim Dalton; transferred by Sirmick and Charlie Miller; source: SBD Master Reel (7" two track @ 7 1/2 ips - recorded by Betty Cantor) > PCM501ES @ 44.055 kHz > DAT (44k) - From the Tim Dalton collection. [3]. Also: Tape flip in Drums was patched using shnid 98781 [3]
- **gd1978-04-16.149552.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by PCM provided by anonymous, while hiding out away from the Bay Area. Edited & Mastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel April 15, 2020; source: Source: Betty Cantor's SBD Reel Master > Beta tape > Beta VCR > PCM [5]. Also: Sony ECM-54P cassettes supplied the second set, with emphasis decoded and DC offset removed; PCM clone created via 601esd and SPDIF, avoiding analog-to-analog copying [5]
- **gd1978-04-16.148566.sony.54p.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 x Sony ECM-54P mics > Sony 158 [6]. Also: Charlie Miller handled the transfer and coordinated the release effort [6]
- **gd1978-04-16.sbd.cantor.motb.81457.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Jim Goldman; source: Betty Soundboard [9]. Also: Jim Goldman found an Ampex reel labeled GD Huntington in a box of tapes; The tape was transferred using computer recording, as no 24/48 recorders were available then [9]
- **gd78-04-16.sbd.lai.292.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1978-04-16 Huntington Civic Center, Huntington, WV, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1978-04-16-huntington-civic-center-huntington-wv-usa/) [31]
- Poster by NetService: [The Grateful Dead live at Huntington Civic Centre, West Virginia – 16 April 1978 – Grateful Ted](https://gratefulted.co.uk/reviews/grateful-dead-live-huntington-civic-centre-west-virginia-16-april-1978/) [32]
